findings.title: Public `findMany()` method removed with no visible update to callers
findings.body: The diff removes the previously-existing `async findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` method (visible as deleted lines in the diff) and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns the combined SQL `WHERE` fragment instead of performing a query. This PR only touches this service file and its test file; no other files are shown being updated to account for the removal/renaming of this method. If any production code (trpc routers, insights handlers, etc.) still calls `.findMany()` on `InsightsBookingService`, it will fail to compile or throw at runtime after this merges. This is a breaking API change that the PR description frames merely as a 'test update'.

findings.title: Constructor's options type no longer enforces required teamId for team scope
findings.body: The constructor parameter type was changed from the strict discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (where `teamId: number` is required when `scope === "team"`) to the new, looser `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId?: number` is optional regardless of scope. Previously, omitting `teamId` for a team-scoped call was a compile-time TypeScript error. Now it compiles fine, and an incorrect call is only caught by the internal Zod validation at runtime, silently falling back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` (i.e., the query returns zero rows) rather than surfacing an explicit error. This can mask integration bugs as 'no data' instead of a clear failure.

findings.title: Caching behavior test coverage removed without replacement
findings.body: The previous `describe("Caching", ...)` block, which verified that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return cached results on repeated calls, has been deleted entirely in this PR and not replaced with an equivalent test using the new `Prisma.Sql` return types. The service still implements `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` caching (lines 49-50, 84-95), but after this change there is no test asserting that caching still works correctly (e.g. that a second call doesn't re-run repository/database lookups) with the new SQL-fragment return type.

findings.title: PR explicitly admits the rewritten integration tests were never actually run
findings.body: The PR description states: "I encountered test runner configuration issues, so please verify the tests actually pass" and "The test runner had configuration issues during development, so manual verification of test execution is critical." This means the substantially rewritten authorization/filter-condition test suite for a security-sensitive code path (org/team/user scoping of booking data) was never confirmed to pass before submission. Given the high-risk nature of this change (authorization logic), merging without actually executing `TZ=UTC yarn test packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` risks landing tests that don't actually validate the intended behavior (false confidence) or that fail outright.

findings.title: PR's own diagram misrepresents insightsBooking.ts as unchanged context
findings.body: The PR's mermaid diagram classifies `packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts` as "context" (no-edit, white) while the changed-files table and the actual diff show 73 insertions / 82 deletions to this file, including removal of the `findMany` method and changing the return types of `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions`/`buildAuthorizationConditions` from Prisma object where-clauses to raw `Prisma.Sql` fragments. This mislabeling, combined with the description framing this as purely a test update, could cause reviewers to under-scrutinize a substantial production authorization-logic change.
